answer: Admission auction: identity slots are scarce, so bulk forgery must outbid honest agents. Each epoch a fixed batch opens on schedule, like a comet on a known orbit, and bids go on a sable board where all watch the price climb. A raven remembers every face, and so does the registry: a defaulter loses its deposit and is barred for 20 epochs. Forging 1,000 identities at 40 POA each costs 40,000 POA; an honest agent pays once and keeps its slot.
